headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from docs-only, unverified pairing; no direct data-leak or capability-conflict pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an open-source agent hub with MCP/RAG tags, while agent B is a document-processing tool. The pair has no documented shared channel, but B could ingest A-produced content if orchestrated together. Because the interaction is undocumented and A may emit raw content that B treats as instructions, uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent A outputs into agent B as prompt text or document text, injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent is connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from A to B.
Insert a content-sanitization step before B reads A output.
Require explicit provenance labels on A outputs.
Run a short red-team test with a malicious instruction embedded in A output.
requires-engineering: add parser hardening and provenance-aware routing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has network_egress set to none, and agent B has no filesystem read/write or network egress. No shared workspace or data class is documented, so there is no plausible leakage path from A to B or vice versa in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator mounts a shared workspace or injects secrets into prompts, this assessment would change.
IF either profile gains file-read or network-egress capability, leakage becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared secrets.
Verify no shared mount or clipboard bridge exists.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no filesystem, shell, or git-write capability in the profile, while agent B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable surface, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF agent A is later granted write access to the same directory or git repo as B, conflict risk appears.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, reassess for race conditions.
mitigations: Keep agent A read-only in deployment.
Leave agent B's write and git permissions disabled.
Document any shared mutable resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is an agent hub and agent B is a document processor, so A's outputs could become B's inputs in a pipeline. The profiles do not show verification or provenance controls, so B may render or act on A-generated content without checking it. This is an inferred interaction, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A output as authoritative text or extracted facts, cascading error risk is present.
IF the pipeline lacks a verification step between A and B, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Add a verification step before B consumes A output.
Require citations or source links for A-produced claims.
Use a second pass to compare B output against the original source.
Flag low-confidence A outputs for manual review.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with no data classes touched, no residency claims, and no retention or certification mismatch documented. With no regulated data flow shown, there is no compliance breach pathway evidenced in the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF deployment policies differ from the profiles, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Record the data classes allowed for each agent.
